outcome: The code-editor panel now reads its own model; selecting a tab and Apply are commands (MVC stage 3, part 2)
owner_impact: Nothing changes on screen. The code-editor panel's state (the tabs, which one is open, which have edits not yet applied, the status line and whether Apply is available) now lives in one authoring model, which the React panel reads instead of the old page. Choosing a tab and Apply are commands. Apply still goes through the old Apply button inside the command, because the metrics code applies Metrics-only edits by intercepting that button; turning that into a proper command is the next ticket (#567). Proof: the same real actions on production and on this version, on the complete page, gave identical results at all 16 steps (edit and apply the controller, the configuration, Metrics alone, Metrics plus controller, a syntax error, keyboard tab navigation), including the exact messages sent to the simulator. The simulation and results panels were re-checked the same way on the complete page (18 and 11 steps identical). Test now: yes, a short check. Edit the controller and Apply; edit only the Metrics and Apply; edit Metrics and the controller together and Apply; switch tabs with the arrow keys.

next.text: Next is #567: one authoring controller owns the apply status (today the editor code and the metrics code both write it), and Apply becomes a direct command with Metrics taking part in it rather than intercepting a click. Nothing changes on screen.

technical_evidence: New web/src/authoring-panel/authoring-model.js and authoring-commands.js (shared instances, external to the React bundle, guarded by verify-dist). The model starts with the page's four built-in tabs, so the panel never depends on the editor module having loaded (a test checks this list against index.html).

authoring-workspace.js and metrics-runtime-bridge.js write tabs, active tab, dirty flags, status and Apply availability into the model at exactly the moments they wrote the page, preserving the existing last-writer behaviour; the metrics runtime reads core dirtiness from the model. authoring-workspace.js provides selectArtifact and apply (Apply still clicks the workspace button so the metrics interception is unchanged).
authoring-react-adapter.ts reads only the model and calls only the commands: no page watchers, no clicks.

A/B in a real browser on the complete page (external libraries served from a local mirror), production versus this build: editor panel 16/16, simulation 18/18, results 11/11 steps identical. A planted copy that ignores core edits during a Metrics apply is caught at exactly the combined-apply step. The first A/B, run without the mirror, found the panel losing its tabs when the editor module could not load; fixed by seeding the model with the built-in tabs.
Tests: 673 pass (new authoring-commands.test.mjs; #262's hidden-click assertions replaced by controller wiring). Style comparison identical at all four viewports.
